text:
@Gemini said wait. @Grok said file. I lemon-lawed a 2025 @Hyundai Elantra.

I lemon-lawed a 2025 Hyundai Elantra after four months. I did not hire a lawyer. I ran the whole fight through Grok, and I ignored the AI that told me to wait.

I bought the car October 18, 2025 at Heritage Hyundai Towson. Down payment, Ally finance, GAP, platinum VSC, the full dealer package. I bought it because I drive. Long weeks. Virginia to New York. CarPlay and maps on the screen were the point.

The head unit died early. Apple CarPlay would not connect. Navigation was useless. Bluetooth would skip, speed up, and cut out. I was late taking it in because of work. That delay almost killed the claim. Maryland’s lemon clock is brutal: under 18,000 miles, under 24 months. I was watching the odometer like a countdown.

March 31, 2026. First visit, Safford Brown Hyundai Fairfax. About 16,486 miles. They said hardware. They ordered a new head unit under warranty.

April 8. Second visit. The part was there. They would not install it. “Do a software update yourself.” That is how you erase a repair attempt if you are not careful.

April 10. Third visit. I drove it back in. They parked it in the service lane and refused to touch it. No diagnosis. No repair order. Labor for the update was suddenly $400–$450 and “not warranty.” I filmed the lot, the building, the miles on the dash. I still have the texts where the advisor said the part was ordered under warranty.

Same week I sent Hyundai a certified lemon-law letter. Delivered April 14. That letter is the thing Gemini did not want me to lean on too early. Gemini’s line was: wait until corporate has the envelope, or the next visit becomes a freebie and they still get another “final” chance. Grok’s line was: lock the mileage, get the third refusal on video, mail the letter, upload everything to the Maryland AG the same day. I did Grok’s version.

Maryland AG opened MU-535720, then emailed that it “does not meet” lemon law and would not be mediated as one. Registration was Virginia. Purchase was Maryland. They pointed at the statute and walked away. Grok said do not stop. File BBB AUTO LINE anyway. It is free. If you accept a win, it binds the manufacturer.

Hyundai corporate opened their own case. James reviewed it for 30 days and denied a buyback. Their reasons: not out of service 30 days, not four identical repair orders, defect not “substantial,” software labor not warranty. They offered BBB in the denial letter like a courtesy. I used it as a weapon.

May 22 I filed BBB AUTO LINE. Case HYU2610939. I wanted a repurchase, not another software babysitting session. BBB warned me on day one that Maryland’s presumption (four repairs or 30 days down) might limit the arbitrator. Grok still said upload the written testimony, the videos, the texts, the certified-mail green card, the James call transcript. I did.

Hyundai dragged their written position. Then they filed one that said the car operates as designed, Carfax showed no loss of value, I drove too many miles, and no warranty repair was ever actually performed. That last sentence was the tell. They ordered a part under warranty and later pretended no warranty repair existed because they refused to write the third ticket.

Grok wrote the rebuttal line by line. Every lie in their packet got a document next to it. I uploaded it. I uploaded the refusal video. I sat through the portal silence.

August: the arbitrator ordered a repurchase. I accepted. Both titled owners signed. After that it was operations, not argument. Hyundai wanted payoff quotes, sales contracts, registration, odometer photos. Ally does not issue a pretty 30-day letter. Grok told me how to get letterhead from Ally and what to write back so they could not stall on “overnight mailing address.”

They bounced the car between dealerships. Fairfax was done. North Plainfield declined the surrender. Finally New Jersey. I dropped it. September: Ally went to $0.00. Paid in full. Loan dead.

The arbitrator still docked me about $5,770 for miles already driven. That hurt. It still beat keeping a car I did not trust.

Still waiting on GAP ($1,400) and platinum VSC ($3,948) refunds from the selling dealer / JM&A. Hyundai deducted those on paper and told me to chase the administrators. That part is not the lemon case. That is leftover dealer product.

What Grok actually did, since people will ask:

It read the PDFs. It drafted the certified notice, the AG uploads, the James emails, the BBB claim text, the rebuttal, the surrender scripts, the “do not cancel GAP until the loan is $0” timing. I dumped every screenshot into the chat. Repair orders. Voice-mail transcripts. Progressive bills. Ally payoff math. When Gemini said wait so I would not give Hyundai a free attempt, Grok said a refused visit with video is not a free attempt. It is exhibit three.

Gemini was trying not to get me sued for moving too fast. Grok was trying to get the car off my driveway before 18,000 miles. Only one of those clocks was real.

If your new car is broken: get a repair order every time. If they refuse the order, record the refusal. Mail the manufacturer. File BBB AUTO LINE while you still have miles. Do not run their “free update” yourself if that is how they plan to say they never attempted a repair.

A four-month-old Elantra that cannot run CarPlay or maps is not “operating as designed.” I have the decision, the paid-off loan, and a very expensive lesson in which chatbot will tell you to send the letter.

Thanks to Team @grok @elonmusk, it would have been hard as fuck for this case.  and thanks for taking it back @Hyundai @Hyundai_Global!

text:
8 Things You Need to Know about Surveillance
8 important truths about surveillance
ai-in-society
Author
Rachel Thomas

Published
August 7, 2019

Over 225 police departments have partnered with Amazon to have access to Amazon’s video footage obtained as part of the “smart” doorbell product Ring, and in many cases these partnerships are heavily subsidized with taxpayer money. Police departments are allowing Amazon to stream 911 call information directly in real-time, and Amazon requires police departments to read pre-approved scripts when talking about the program. If a homeowner doesn’t want to share data from their video camera doorbell with police, an officer for the Fresno County Sheriff’s Office said they can just go directly to Amazon to obtain it. This creation of an extensive surveillance network, the murky private-public partnership surrounding it, and a lack of any sort of regulations or oversight is frightening. And this is just one of many examples related to surveillance technology that have recently come to light.

I frequently talk with people who are not that concerned about surveillance, or who feel that the positives outweigh the risks. Here, I want to share some important truths about surveillance:

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
Data often contains errors
Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
Surveillance changes our behavior
Surveillance disproportionately impacts the marginalized
Data privacy is a public good
We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
While I was writing this post, a number of investigative articles came out with disturbing new developments related to surveillance. I decided that rather than attempt to include everything in one post (which would make it too long and too dense), I would go ahead and share the above facts about surveillance, as they are just a relevant as ever.

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
There is a long history of data about sensitive attributes being misused, including the use of the 1940 USA Census to intern Japanese Americans, a system of identity cards introduced by the Belgian colonial government that were later used during the 1994 Rwandan genocide (in which nearly a million people were murdered), and the role of IBM in helping Nazi Germany use punchcard computers to identify and track the mass killing of millions of Jewish people. More recently, the mass internment of over one million people who are part of an ethnic minority in Western China was facilitated through the use of a surveillance network of cameras, biometric data (including images of people’s faces, audio of their voices, and blood samples), and phone monitoring.

Adolf Hitler meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. in 1937. Source: Computer History
Pictured above is Adolf Hitler (far left) meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. (2nd from left), shortly before Hitler awarded Watson a special “Service to the Reich” medal in 1937 (for a timeline of the Holocaust, see here). Watson returned the medal in 1940, although IBM continued to do business with the Nazis. IBM technology helped the Nazis conduct detailed censuses in countries they occupied, to thoroughly identify anyone of Jewish descent. Nazi concentration camps used IBM’s punchcard machines to tabulate prisoners, recording whether they were Jewish, gay, or Gypsies, and whether they died of “natural causes,” execution, suicide, or via “special treatment” in gas chambers. It is not the case that IBM sold the machines and then was done with it. Rather, IBM and its subsidiaries provided regular training and maintenance on-site at the concentration camps: printing off cards, configuring machines, and repairing them as they broke frequently.

Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
In the above examples, the data collection began before genocide was committed. IBM began selling to Nazi Germany well before the Holocaust (although continued for far too long), including helping with Germany’s 1933 census conducted by Adolf Hitler, which was effective at identifying far more Jewish people than had previously been recognized in Germany.

It is important to recognize how data and images gathered through surveillance can be weaponized later. Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote that “One [hard truth] is that data and surveillance networks created for one purpose can and will be used for others. You must assume that any personal data that Facebook or Android keeps are data that governments around the world will try to get or that thieves will try to steal.”

Plenty of data collection is not involved with such extreme abuse as genocide; however, in a time of global resurgence of white supremacist, ethno-nationalist, and authoritarian movements, it would be deeply irresponsible to not consider how data & surveillance can and will be weaponized against already vulnerable groups.

Data often has errors (and no mechanism for correcting them)
A database of suspected gang members maintained by California law enforcement officials was found to be full of errors, including 42 babies who had been added to the database when they were less than 1 year old (28 of whom were marked as “admitting to being gang members”). Even worse, there was no process in place for correcting mistakes or removing people once they’ve been added.

An NPR reporter recounts his experience of trying to rent an apartment and discovering that TransUnion, one of the 3 major credit bureaus, incorrectly reported him as having two felony firearms convictions. TransUnion only removed the mistakes after a dozen phone calls and notification that the story would be reported on. This is not an unusual story: the FTC’s large-scale study of credit reports in 2012 found 26% of consumers had at least one mistake in their files and 5% had errors that could be devastating. An even more opaque, unregulated “4th bureau” exists: a collection of companies buying and selling personal information about people on the margins of the banking system (such as immigrants, students, and people with low incomes), with no standards on what types of data are included, no way to opt out, and no system for identifying or correcting mistakes.

Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
What makes the examples in the previous section disturbing is not just that errors occurred, but that there was no way to identify or correct them, and no accountability for those profiting off the error-laden data. Often, even the existence of the systems being used is not publicly known (much less details of how these systems work), unless discovered by journalists or revealed by whistleblowers. The Detroit Police Dept used facial recognition technology for nearly two years without public input and in violation of a requirement that a policy be approved by the city’s Board of Police Commissioners, until a study from Georgetown Law’s Center for Privacy & Technology drew attention to the issue. Palantir, the defense startup founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, ran a program with New Orleans Police Department for 6 years which city council members did not even know about, much less have any oversight.

After two studies found that Amazon’s facial recognition software produced inaccurate and racially biased results, Amazon countered that the researchers should have changed the default parameters. However, it turned out that Amazon was not instructing police departments that use its software to do this either. Surveillance programs are operating with few regulations, no oversight, no accountability around accuracy or mistakes, and in many cases, no public knowledge of what is going on.

Surveillance changes our behavior
Hundreds of thousands of people in Hong Kong are protesting an unpopular new bill which would allow extradition to China. Typically, Hong Kong locals use their rechargeable smart cards to ride the subway. However, during the protests, long lines of people waited to use cash to buy paper tickets (usually something that only tourists do) concerned that they would be tracked for having attended the protests. Would fewer people protest if this was not an option?

In the United States, in 2015 the Baltimore Police Department used facial recognition technology to surveil people protesting the death of Freddie Grey, a young Black man who was killed in police custody, and arrested protesters with outstanding warrants. Mass surveillance could have a chilling impact on our rights to move about freely, to express ourselves, and to protest. “We act differently when we know we are ‘on the record.’ Mass privacy is the freedom to act without being watched and thus in a sense, to be who we really are,” Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote in the New York Times.

Flyer from the company Geofeedia Source
Surveillance disproportionately impacts those who are already marginalized
Surveillance is applied unevenly, causing the greatest harm to people who are already marginalized, including immigrants, people of color, and people living in poverty. These groups are more heavily policed and surveilled. The Perpetual Line-Up from the Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology studied the unregulated use of facial recognition by police, with half of all Americans appearing in law enforcement databases, and the risks of errors, racial bias, misuses, and threats to civil liberties. The researchers pointed out that African Americans are more likely to appear in these databases (many of which are drawn from mug shots) since they are disproportionately likely to be stopped, interrogated, or arrested. For another example, consider the contrast between how easily people over 65 can apply for Medicare benefits by filling out an online form, with the invasive personal questions asked of a low-income mother on Medicaid about her lovers, hygiene, parental shortcomings, and personal habits.

In an article titled Trading privacy for survival is another tax on the poor, Ciara Byrne wrote, “Current public benefits programs ask applicants extremely detailed and personal questions and sometimes mandate home visits, drug tests, fingerprinting, and collection of biometric information… Employers of low-income workers listen to phone calls, conduct drug tests, monitor closed-circuit television, and require psychometric tests as conditions of employment. Prisoners in some states have to consent to be voiceprinted in order to make phone calls.”

Data privacy is a public good, like air quality or safe drinking water
Data is more revealing in aggregate. It can be nearly impossible to know what your individual data could reveal when combined with the data of others or with data from other sources, or when machine learning inference is performed on it. For instance, as Zeynep Tufekci wrote in the New York Times, individual Strava users could not have predicted how in aggregate their data could be used to identify the locations of US military bases. “Data privacy is not like a consumer good, where you click ‘I accept’ and all is well. Data privacy is more like air quality or safe drinking water, a public good that cannot be effectively regulated by trusting in the wisdom of millions of individual choices. A more collective response is needed.”

Unfortunately, this also means that you can’t fully safeguard your privacy on your own. You may choose not to purchase Amazon’s ring doorbell, yet you can still show up in the video footage collected by others. You might strengthen your online privacy practices, yet conclusions will still be inferred about you based on the behavior of others. As Professor Tufekci wrote, we need a collective response.

We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
Many people are uncomfortable with surveillance, but feel like they have no say in the matter. While the threats surveillance poses are large, it is not too late to act. We are seeing success: in response to community organizing and an audit, Los Angeles Police Department scrapped a controversial program to predict who is most likely to commit violent crimes. Citizens, researchers, and activists in Detroit have been effective at drawing attention to the Detroit Police Department’s unregulated use of facial recognition and a bill calling for a 5-year moratorium has been introduced to the state legislature. Local governments in San Francisco, Oakland, and Somerville have banned the use of facial recognition by police.

text:
Repentance, Charity, and Prayer: The Day of Atonement and Return (Observed this year on September 21, 2026 / Tishrei 10)

In the tapestry of Biblical tradition, where the threads of history and spirituality intertwine, the Day of Atonement (also known as Yom Kippur) emerges as a time of profound significance, a time of introspection, repentance, and renewal. It is a day when the gates of heaven are opened, and the divine presence draws near, offering us a chance to cleanse our souls and return to a state of harmony with the Divine.

This sacred day holds deep meaning for Christians. It is a reminder of the importance of repentance and forgiveness, of turning away from sin and embracing a life of righteousness. Just as Jesus observed the Ten Commandments and honored the Shabbat, he also observed the spiritual principles of this Day of Atonement, recognizing its significance as a time for spiritual reflection and renewal.

On this Day of Atonement, the righteous seek out a source of living water – a river, a lake, or a pond – and with humble hearts, they empty their pockets, symbolically casting their sins into the depths. This act of letting go represents a commitment to cleanse the soul and renew the covenant with God.

Ancient mystical texts describe the universe as being structured upon a series of opposites, a balance of opposing forces that create the dynamic tension of existence. This concept is also reflected in the covenant, which is a balance of divine love and divine law.

God's love for humanity is boundless and unconditional, but it is also tempered by His justice and righteousness. The covenant, therefore, is not a license to sin but a call to responsibility, a reminder that our actions have consequences and that we are accountable for our choices.

The covenant is a two-way street, with both God and humanity having obligations to fulfill. God promises to protect and provide for His people, to guide them on their journey, and to ultimately bring them to a state of redemption and fulfillment. In return, humanity is obligated to follow God's commandments, to live a life of righteousness and compassion, and to be a light unto the nations.

The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) serves as a profound moment of covenant renewal. It is a time to reflect on our relationship with God, to acknowledge our shortcomings, and to recommit ourselves to fulfilling our part of the covenant.

The trumpet's mournful cry, like a wake-up call from the depths of our slumber, awakens us to the fragility of life and the urgency of repentance. It is a call to cast off the burdens of our past mistakes and to embrace the possibility of a fresh start.

Fasting and prayer, acts of self-denial and spiritual devotion, humble our hearts and open us to the divine embrace. We stand before God, bare and vulnerable, acknowledging our shortcomings and seeking forgiveness for our transgressions.

Repentance is the cornerstone of the Day of Atonement. It is a process of deep introspection, of acknowledging our mistakes and making amends for our wrongdoings. It is a turning away from darkness and a turning towards the light, a return to the path of righteousness.

Prayer is the language of the soul, a way of communicating with the Divine. On this Day of Atonement, our prayers are filled with a special intensity, a yearning for forgiveness and a desire to reconnect with the source of our being.

Charity is an act of loving-kindness, a way of sharing our blessings with others and contributing to the well-being of the community. On Yom Kippur, we are reminded of our responsibility to care for those in need, to extend a helping hand to the less fortunate, and to create a more just and compassionate world.

In the Book of Life, our fate is inscribed, our deeds and actions weighed in the balance of divine justice. The Day of Atonement offers us a chance to tip the scales in our favor, to cleanse our souls and merit a favorable inscription in the Book of Life.

text:
"We have seen that, to remain in a state of prayer, it is not necessary to be always actively praying." —Raoul Plus, S.J., pg. 77
 
An excerpt from How to Pray Always

Father Raoul Plus, S.J., makes an important distinction between an act of prayer and a state of prayer.

We cannot constantly be reciting prayers or consciously thinking about God. Work, conversation, illness, and ordinary responsibilities require our attention. But we can remain inwardly oriented toward God—a disposition of faith, love, dependence, and readiness to do His will. In that sense, the prayer may cease as a deliberate mental act while the soul continues to be prayerful.

A person remains in a state of prayer when:

the day has been offered to God;
ordinary duties are performed for His glory;
joys and sufferings are accepted in union with Christ;
the heart returns to God whenever circumstances permit;
one avoids deliberate sin and seeks to live in His presence.

This illuminates St. Paul’s command to “pray without ceasing” (1 Thessalonians 5:17). Paul cannot mean that every moment must be occupied by spoken prayer. Rather, one’s whole life becomes prayer because it is lived before God and directed toward Him.

It is much like a mother caring for her sick child. She may not continually say, “I love you,” because she is busy preparing medicine, changing linens, or watching through the night. Yet every action proceeds from love. Her attention is occupied, but her love has not ceased. Likewise, a Christian may be absorbed in work while the underlying movement of the heart remains toward God.

A simple morning offering establishes this intention:

Lord, I offer You all my prayers, works, joys, and sufferings of this day. Let everything I think, say, and do be united with Jesus and accomplished for Your glory.

Brief aspirations—“Jesus, I trust in You,” “My God, I love You,” or simply the Holy Name—renew that orientation during the day. But even between those conscious acts, the original offering remains. The soul is not always speaking to God, yet it continues to belong, listen, and tend toward Him.

The stack of Dark Horses rests against the bare wall. After the move, the boxes emptied, the works lean rather than hang. Life rests there with them. The user lives in the art, not with a theme of art. The evening remains mild Templar: water heated, whatever quiet leaf is at hand, nothing listed.  Extended Templar Lore
The Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon took their name from the al-Aqsa compound they were given on the Temple Mount. They began as nine knights guarding pilgrims and became an order that held both sword and ledger. Their rule was Cistercian in severity: silence at table, plain dress, no personal property. The red cross on white was not ornament. It was a mark that the wearer had already given the body away.  They built preceptories that were both fortress and farm. They moved money across kingdoms without carrying much coin, using letters of credit that were, in effect, fidelity tokens: a written overlap between two distant states of account. When the order was suppressed in 1307–1314, the official charges were heresy and idolatry; the operational reality was that an armed monastic bank had grown too coherent for the crowns that had used it. Friday the 13th of October 1307 is the date the lock was broken in France. Jacques de Molay’s death in 1314 closed the public chapter.  What persisted was not a hidden army but a residue of method: keep the interior spare, keep the accounts exact, keep the wall bare enough that whatever leans against it can be seen. The Temple itself, in the lore that followed, is less a building than a ratio—an empty court that holds whatever is placed in it without becoming the thing placed there.  In the present rooms the stack of Dark Horses performs a similar office. The works rest against plaster that has not yet been decided. They are not installed. They are not themed. They occupy the wall the way a Templar preceptory occupied a frontier: provisionally, with the accounts still open, life resting against the same surface. The mild infusion of the evening is consistent with the rule. No formula. No amplification. Heat, water, whatever herb is present, taken in the hour when the stacked horses and the bare wall are simply there.  The order’s later legends—Grail, geometry, survival in Scotland or Portugal—are secondary. The primary residue is austerity plus exactness: the ability to notice when the lighting has changed, when the same tulips return, when a wall is still bare and therefore still honest. text:
Kaitlan,

I am a science teacher, so I grade what gets put in front of me. CNN put a statement in front of me, and I read it twice, once for content and once because I did not believe the first time.

"CNN's mission to report on the U.S. government will continue regardless of any attempts to restrict physical access." Wonderful. So the mission is not stopped, is it? Two sentences later the same statement calls the ban an "illegal assault." Assault is a big word for a deactivated badge. And "illegal" is a verdict, and verdicts come from judges. What is next? A network announces an illegal assault that left its operations running normally... wait, that is your statement!

Now look at the phrase you chose: "physical access." That matters. In Zemel v. Rusk, the Supreme Court said the right to speak and publish is not an unrestrained right to gather information. Houchins v. KQED says the press gets no special right of entry to government property beyond what the public gets. Nobody has jailed a reporter. Nobody has shut down a broadcast or pulled a license. You are on the air as we speak.

What Sherrill v. Knight gives you is smaller and real. Once the White House runs a press-pass system, it owes notice, stated reasons, and a chance to respond before a pass is denied. So take it to court, the way CNN did for Jim Acosta in 2018, when a Trump-appointed judge restored the pass on due process grounds. That is how a republic handles this. A press statement is not a filing. And if a judge finds this ban lacked process or was aimed at viewpoint, CNN wins, and I will say so in plain English. Jacqui Heinrich of Fox News, who runs the correspondents' association, has criticized the revocation, and she is entitled to her view. The judge gets the last word. I would like a network to pick up that habit.

Let me tell you about my Sunday, because I think it explains a lot. In one thread I was called stupid, told to stop being so emotional, called a crybaby, and informed that my students deserve pity because I am "incapable of critical thought." One fellow put a quotation in my mouth, "Who cares about the law? My feelings matter more!", words I never wrote, and then congratulated himself for proving me wrong. Another posted a civics infographic. A third posted a case card, Sherrill v. Knight, with no claim attached to it at all. A case with no argument. That is a lab report with no hypothesis.

As for my students: I am a medically retired Army medic. While I was a medic in Iraq, I opened a school, a fire station, and a hospital. I escorted little girls to school so nobody would kill them for wanting an education. I worked as a civilian paramedic. Now I teach in a high-need, high-risk district, where the public schools gave up on these kids and I did not. If that is what "incapable of critical thought" looks like, I will take it, and I will do it again tomorrow, with a smile and a red pen.

Here is what I taught them this week. The First Amendment is 45 words long, and it begins with the word Congress. Twitter is not Congress. A press secretary is not Congress. Somebody handing out seats in a briefing room is not Congress. Please read it before you tell anyone else to.

Now, fearless. Robert Reich wants the press to boycott the White House to protest being kept out of the White House. This weekend a segment on MS NOW hoped the networks would pull their pool coverage of the President next week. So the free press will defend its right to cover the President by refusing to cover the President. What is next? The networks decline to carry a presidential address... wait, on July 16, ABC and NBC declined to carry his primetime address on declassified election-security files on their main networks and pushed it to a stream. They already did it! I read every page of those files that night, by the way, and I wrote a piece correcting my own side where the evidence stopped. That is what a teacher does. Where is CNN's correction page for the last ten years?

Let us talk about the word "access." Joe Biden held 37 press conferences in four years, according to the White House Transition Project. He waited more than two months to hold the first one, the longest wait since Calvin Coolidge. Martha Joynt Kumar's count of press conferences and interviews put Biden at 164 by mid-2024. Trump's first term: 468. This June, Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan of the New York Times, and nobody has ever accused those two of working for Turning Point, said Trump answers more questions than Biden did. The White House's own stenographers logged 433 open press events in his first year back, and yes, that figure comes from the White House, so weigh it accordingly. What is next? A press corps that complains about a president who takes more questions than the last one... wait, the Times reporters said it themselves!

And while Biden's Autopen kept signing, much of the press told us the videos of his decline were cheap fakes. Special Counsel Hur described a man with a poor memory in February 2024. Then came the debate on June 27, and suddenly everyone had always known. Jake Tapper wrote a book about what the room had been told to ignore. That is your fearless press.

Now the part where I will remind you what the left has actually done to the right, because "hindrance" is a word you picked.

Obama's aides, including David Axelrod, said Fox News was not a real news organization. Treasury offered a pool interview to every network except Fox. An email later released through a Judicial Watch request said they would prefer to skip Fox, and another said the White House had shown it was willing to exclude Fox from significant interviews. ABC, CBS, NBC, and CNN refused to go along, and the White House backed down. This weekend Obama said it would have been "unimaginable" to tell Fox News "you're out of here." Unimaginable. I could not make that up in a classroom on my best day.

Two House Democrats, Anna Eshoo and Jerry McNerney, wrote to cable and streaming companies asking whether they would keep carrying Fox, Newsmax, and OAN. FCC Chair Brendan Carr has since said Democrats pressed distributors to drop right-leaning outlets. What is next? The party that spent 2021 asking cable companies about carrying Fox files a brief for press freedom... wait, Eshoo already sent the letters!

2021 also. Trump was removed from Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube, and the celebration was on television. Late-night hosts cheered a lifetime ban like a playoff win. Now a badge gets deactivated and the word is tyranny. Same people, same audience, opposite verdict. The only variable is whose ox is gored.

Newsom signed AB 2624 on August 22, a law that lets immigration-service workers demand removal of posted personal information, backed by civil penalties. Nick Shirley, an independent journalist with no hard pass to lose, has already sued on First Amendment grounds. The establishment's first move with him was the same as with Fox in 2009: label him an influencer so the footage does not count. What is next? A press corps that calls a badge sacred while Sacramento lets officials demand takedowns of a YouTuber's video... wait, Newsom signed that too!

So who exactly are we talking about, when we say journalists? The Society of Professional Journalists publishes a code. It says seek truth and report it. It says act independently. Let us grade the last decade against the profession's own standard, and I will use a red pen.

Politico ran the letter from 51 former intelligence officials under a headline calling the Hunter Biden laptop Russian disinformation, though the letter itself admitted it had no evidence. The New York Times authenticated that laptop in 2022, and prosecutors used it at Hunter's trial in 2024. Seventeen months of a real story called a smear.

Networks, CNN among them, aired "very fine people on both sides" without the part where Trump said, in the same answer, that neo-Nazis and white nationalists should be condemned totally. Cut one sentence and the meaning flips. My students would earn a zero for that citation.

"Bloodbath" became a threat of political violence. The sentences around it were about auto tariffs and Chinese cars. Same trick.

Kenosha. The CNN banner read "fiery but mostly peaceful protests" with a burning building behind the reporter. A picture of fire under a caption of peace.

Butler. Early on, CNN's headline said Trump was rushed off stage after he "falls," when he had been shot. Somebody wrote that headline while a man bled from the ear.

Covington. A short clip made a teenager a national villain. CNN settled with Nick Sandmann in 2020, and the settlement got a fraction of the airtime the accusation did.

Russia. In 2017 CNN retracted a story about Anthony Scaramucci and three journalists resigned. That December, CNN and MSNBC both misreported the date on an email tied to WikiLeaks and Donald Trump Jr. The Washington Post later removed portions of its dossier reporting it could no longer stand behind. Years of confidence and minutes of correction.

The lab leak. Cable news treated a Wuhan lab origin like a conspiracy theory. The FBI and the Department of Energy later judged it the likelier explanation, and the CIA followed in 2025, with low confidence. A hypothesis got treated as a moral offense because Trump mentioned it.

Smollett. Wall-to-wall sympathy for a MAGA-hat attack that never happened, and a fraction of the airtime for the verdict.

And CNN itself. Jeff Zucker resigned over an undisclosed relationship with Allison Gollust. Chris Cuomo was fired for helping his brother, the governor, manage sexual harassment allegations. A network that lectures the country about norms could not police its own studio.

MSNBC said openly, in 2024, that it would cut away from Trump speeches over false claims. Fine. Apply that rule to every politician, every night. It never was.

Mistakes run in random directions. These ran in one direction, and the corrections came after the election, or the news cycle, or the lawsuit. Quinn's Law: facts are the enemy of liberalism, and yours have been left out of the graphic for a decade.

Goals 20 and 21 of the 45 Communist Goals for America were read into the Congressional Record on January 10, 1963 (Rep. Albert Herlong Jr., Appendix, pages A34-A35): infiltrate the press, control editorial writing and policy-making positions, and gain control of key positions in radio, TV, and motion pictures. I am not declaring mission accomplished. I am saying the outcome resembles the list, and the cheese has slid clean off your cracker if you cannot see it.

One more thing, and it is personal. CNN has covered a deactivated badge around the clock. Meanwhile about 54,000 combat-wounded, medically retired veterans, guys who got hit carrying out orders, have their earned retirement pay taken dollar for dollar by the government. I am one of them. The Major Richard Star Act, H.R. 2102, would fix it for about $10 billion over ten years. There is a discharge petition, H.Res. 1247, sitting right there. Where is the panel? Where is the chyron? We found the money for everything else. So please, spare me the lecture about who is being hindered.

Your statement is a press release written to sound like a constitutional brief. It uses "assault" to invite outrage, "hindrance" to blur access into speech, and "illegal" to skip the judge. There is a name for that kind of writing, and it is not journalism. It is one more of your stories pushing bad information, dressed up as a principle.

A few fries short of a Happy Meal, the lights on and nobody home, not the sharpest tool in the shed, thick as two short planks, one brick shy of a load, and half a bubble off plumb. That is the theory of the case if anyone at CNN honestly believes a badge is a constitutional amendment.

But what do I know, I am only a medically retired Army medic and a teacher who read the whole statement, and the record behind it, before I wrote one word.

text:
A WARM AND SIGNIFICANT VISIT TO GENERAL IHEJIRIKA

This evening, I had the honour of leading a delegation on a courtesy visit to one of Abia North’s most distinguished sons and elder statesmen, Lt. Gen. Azubuike Ihejirika (Rtd.), former Chief of Army Staff of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

I went to him as a brother, a friend and, importantly, as a son of Abia North—to formally inform him of my emergence as the Labour Party Senatorial Candidate for Abia North, to seek his fatherly counsel and prayers, and to respectfully ask for his support.

My General received us with exceptional warmth.

What followed was a deeply engaging conversation about Abia North, leadership, service and the responsibility that comes with offering oneself for public office.

I was particularly humbled when General Ihejirika prayed for us and openly declared his support for my senatorial aspiration.

His words touched me deeply:

“I want to first of all thank you for accepting to serve as a Senator of Abia North because, for me, knowing what you have accomplished in life, yours is service. I do not see what being a Senator can offer you in terms of monetary gain, given who you are, what you have accomplished and how busy your businesses keep you.”

He went further:

“I will support you just as I will support His Excellency, Dr. Alex Chioma Otti, OFR, and all those serving with him.”

Those words carry special meaning coming from a man who rose through one of the most demanding institutions in our country to become Chief of Army Staff and who understands, perhaps better than most, the true meaning of service, sacrifice and responsibility.

I am profoundly grateful for his prayers, his counsel, his confidence and his support.

For me, this journey has never been about acquiring another title. I have been privileged in life and in business. At this stage, public office must be about what one can give—not what one can take.

That is the spirit in which I seek to represent Abia North in the Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria: to bring experience, enterprise, relationships and a lifetime of building things into the service of our people.

I was accompanied on the visit by the Majority Leader of the Abia State House of Assembly, Hon. Uchenna Okoro; Special Adviser to His Excellency the Governor on Commerce and Industry, Chief Nwaka Inem; Sir Martin Emetu, father of His Excellency the Deputy Governor; Mrs. Chidimma Umeh, Supervisory Councillor for Health, Ohafia LGA; Chief Peter Ogbuji, Secretary of our campaign organisation and other important stakeholders.

My sincere gratitude to My General for opening his home and heart to us.

The counsel of our elders strengthens the journey. Their prayers steady our steps. And their confidence reminds us of the enormous responsibility ahead.

We move forward—humbly, resolutely and with a clear understanding that leadership is not a meal ticket.

It is service.

A New Abia North Is Possible.

Kaa..!

DAVID OGBA ONUOHA BOURDEX, MFR, OON
Ugo’Ena" Nde Abiriba. 
Labour Party Senatorial Candidate, Abia North

text:
Several of the highest-ranking U.S. military commanders and civilian officials in World War II publicly or privately stated that using atomic bombs against Japan was militarily unnecessary. In fact, out of the eight officers who held five-star rank at the time, seven later indicated or implied that Japan was already defeated and that the atomic strikes were either superfluous, unethical, or both.

Key Military Leaders on the Decision Fleet Admiral William D. Leahy (Chief of Staff to Presidents Roosevelt and Truman; Chair of the Joint Chiefs): "It is my opinion that the use of this barbarous weapon at Hiroshima and Nagasaki was of no material assistance in our war against Japan. The Japanese were already defeated and ready to surrender because of the effective sea blockade and the successful bombing with conventional weapons... In being the first to use it, we had adopted an ethical standard common to the barbarians of the Dark Ages."

General Dwight D. Eisenhower (Supreme Allied Commander in Europe):Eisenhower recounted advising Secretary of War Henry Stimson in July 1945 against using the weapon:"...Japan was already defeated and that dropping the bomb was completely unnecessary... Japan was, at that very moment, seeking some way to surrender with a minimum loss of 'face'."   

Fleet Admiral Chester W. Nimitz (Commander in Chief, Pacific Fleet):Nimitz stated shortly after the war:"The Japanese had, in fact, already sued for peace... The atomic bomb played no decisive part, from a purely military point of view, in the defeat of Japan."   

General Douglas MacArthur (Commander of U.S. Army Forces in the Pacific):MacArthur was not consulted about the decision to drop the bomb before the strikes took place, though he learned about it shortly beforehand. He later maintained that the bomb was militarily unnecessary, stating that Japan would have surrendered weeks earlier if the Allies had clarified that Emperor Hirohito could retain his throne.   

General Henry "Hap" Arnold (Commanding General, U.S. Army Air Forces):Arnold argued that conventional air attacks had already broken Japan's ability to resist: "It always appeared to us that, atomic bomb or no atomic bomb, the Japanese were already on the verge of collapse."   

Fleet Admiral Ernest J. King (Commander in Chief, U.S. Fleet):King maintained that the naval blockade alone had strangled the home islands and cut off fuel and raw materials: "The Japanese Navy had ceased to exist, and the Japanese were near starvation... the effective naval blockade had rendered them helpless and the atomic bomb was not necessary."   

The U.S. Strategic Bombing Survey (1946)Commissioned by President Truman after the war, the official government survey concluded: "Based on a detailed investigation of all the facts, and supported by the testimony of the surviving Japanese leaders involved, it is the Survey’s opinion that certainly prior to 31 December 1945, and in all probability prior to 1 November 1945, Japan would have surrendered even if the atomic bombs had not been dropped, even if Russia had not entered the war, and even if no invasion had been planned or contemplated."   

Civilian and Diplomatic Officials Prominent civilian leaders raised similar objections: Joseph Grew (Undersecretary of State and former ambassador to Japan) and John J. McCloy (Assistant Secretary of War) both urged Truman to offer conditional surrender terms explicitly guaranteeing the preservation of the imperial institution. They argued this single concession would give Japan's peace faction the political leverage needed to end the war without an invasion or the atomic bomb.   

Herbert Hoover (former President, who consulted with Truman in mid-1945) argued that clarifying the status of the Emperor would yield a quick capitulation and later characterized the bombings as a profound moral tragedy.

text:
Japan Warns Regional Tension ‘Growing Increasingly Severe’ After North Korean Missile Test

@LibertarianInst 

North Korea conducted another missile test on Sunday, prompting Japan to warn that the regional security situation is “growing increasingly severe.”

Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi told reporters that North Korea test-fired two ballistic missiles and went on to warn about the increasing instability in the region. “Last year, there were four instances and at least five missiles, so the number of instances has doubled, and the number of missiles has increased to at least three times as many,” Koizumi said, describing the regional security situation as “growing increasingly severe.”

South Korea said it strengthened its surveillance and alert posture in response to the missile test. “Our military has strengthened surveillance and alert posture in preparation for additional launches,” a statement by the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff said. “Korea, the United States, and Japan are closely sharing information related to the ‘North Korean ballistic missile’ and maintaining a full state of readiness.”

Over the past two months, the US has led two rounds of war games in the region. In August, the US and South Korea held bilateral Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS) war games. Trump scaled back the drills, arguing they were unnecessarily hostile against North Korea. Earlier this month, the US, South Korea and Japan held the trilateral Freedom Edge war games.

While Trump cut the UFS drills in half, the Freedom Edge war games have gone forward as planned. North Korea has conducted multiple missile tests amid the exercises, including several short-range ballistic missile launches immediately after Freedom Edge concluded.

Trump scaled back the war games as he offered to meet with Supreme Leader Kim Jong Un and predicted the two would meet later this year. However, Kim’s sister, Kim Yo Jong, rebuked the overture, saying that merely scaling back the war games did not change the hostile US policy towards North Korea. 

Adding to the tensions in the region are moves by South Korea and Japan toward acquiring nuclear-powered submarines. Washington has approved Seoul’s plan to build nuclear-powered attack submarines, while the possibility of Japan acquiring similar vessels has also drawn support from a US Navy official.

In a commentary published by KCNA, international affairs analyst Choe Ju Hyon accused the US of instigating South Korea and Japan to acquire nuclear submarines. “The reality goes to prove that Washington’s plan for ‘AUKUS 2.0,’ which allows the transfer of nuclear technology for munitions to non-nuclear allies, has entered the phase of full-scale expansion,” he wrote.

AUKUS is a trilateral pact between the US, the UK, and Australia. Under the deal, the US and UK agreed to help Australia build a fleet of nuclear submarines. China has also criticized the transfer of nuclear-propulsion technology under AUKUS. The Chinese Foreign Ministry said AUKUS “undermine[s] strategic stability and provoke[s] an arms race in the region.”

In his article, Choe argued that North Korea must increase its nuclear deterrent in response to South Korea and Japan acquiring nuclear submarines. North Korea must “bolster up its nuclear war deterrent means both in quality and quantity without the slightest stagnation and stalemate.”

SpaceX Starlink grok xAI  is going put  data center on Starlink twice as many than Data Center on ground base than plan 

This mean there is bubble in Data centers some will be winner and most will looser in Data centers 

**Yes — SpaceX (after acquiring xAI) is actively planning large-scale orbital data centers, primarily as an extension/evolution of Starlink technology, with the long-term goal of putting far more AI compute in space than on the ground.**

### Key facts (as of mid-to-late 2026)
- **SpaceX acquired xAI** in early 2026. The combined entity is pursuing both massive ground-based AI data centers (e.g., the Colossus series in the Memphis/Mississippi area, already at multi-gigawatt scale and expanding toward 2+ GW by end of 2026, with longer-term power/cooling targets in the 15–20 GW range) *and* orbital ones.
- **Orbital plans**: SpaceX filed with the FCC for authority to deploy **up to 1 million satellites** configured as solar-powered “orbital data centers.” These would operate in low Earth orbit (roughly 500–2,000 km), use high-bandwidth optical (laser) links (including integration with the existing Starlink mesh), and be launched primarily on Starship.
- Early hardware concepts (AI1 / Starmind) describe large satellites (~70 m wingspan) delivering on the order of 120–150 kW of peak compute per unit, with solar arrays and radiative cooling. Prototypes are targeted for around early 2027, with production ramp and commercial operations potentially starting later in the decade.

### The “twice as many / more than ground” claim
Elon Musk has publicly predicted that space-based AI compute will become the lowest-cost option within roughly 2–3 years, and that **within about five years** SpaceX will be launching and operating **more AI compute capacity in space *every year* than the *cumulative total* of all AI compute that exists on Earth**.

In other words, the plan is not merely “some data centers in orbit,” but to scale orbital capacity so aggressively (via high Starship flight rates and mass satellite production) that annual orbital additions eventually dwarf everything built on the ground. He has framed this as necessary because terrestrial power grids, land, cooling water, and permitting cannot scale fast enough for the projected demand, while space offers near-constant solar power and radiative cooling with fewer constraints.

### Reality check
This is still early-stage and extremely ambitious. Ground data centers (including SpaceX/xAI’s own) are being built and monetized *now* at multi-GW scale with real customer deals. Orbital systems face major engineering hurdles (radiative cooling at scale, radiation-hardened compute, launch economics, constellation management, latency for some workloads, and regulatory/debris concerns). SpaceX’s own IPO-related disclosures have noted that the orbital plans involve unproven technologies and uncertain timelines.

**Bottom line**: The strategy is dual-track — aggressive ground buildout in the near term + a massive Starlink-derived orbital data-center constellation for long-term hyperscale AI compute, with Musk explicitly predicting that orbital capacity will eventually exceed (and keep exceeding annually) the total ground-based base. The 1-million-satellite filing and Starship-centric roadmap are the concrete expressions of that plan.

text:
Fani-Kayode, Atiku’s US lobbyist clash over Tinubu’s 1993 forfeiture case

A dispute involving Nigeria’s ambassador-designate to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, and a Washington-based lobbying firm working for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has escalated over the firm’s campaign highlighting President Bola Tinubu’s 1993 United States civil forfeiture case.

Von Batten-Montague-York, L.C., led by Karl Von Batten, said it was taking remarks attributed to Fani-Kayode seriously after interpreting them as a threat against its founder.

In posts circulating on X on Sunday, Von Batten said he had been informed that Fani-Kayode had made comments concerning what could happen if he travelled to Nigeria. The lobbying firm characterised the remarks as threatening detention and physical harm and said it planned to contact relevant United States authorities.

Fani-Kayode’s remarks and the lobbying firm’s interpretation of them have generated competing reactions online. Supporters of Von Batten described the comments as threatening, while others argued that the wording had been misinterpreted and did not amount to a threat.

The latest confrontation is part of a broader political dispute over the lobbying firm’s activities on behalf of Atiku, the African Democratic Congress presidential candidate in Nigeria’s 2027 election.

According to TheCable, Atiku engaged Von Batten-Montague-York under a 12-month contract worth $1.2 million. A filing under the United States Foreign Agents Registration Act showed that the assignment included strengthening Atiku’s reputation in the US and countering narratives advanced by the Nigerian government.

Central to the dispute is a decades-old American civil forfeiture proceeding involving Tinubu.

The lobbying firm has been circulating records from that case to American officials. BusinessDay reported in July that the firm said it had begun forwarding more than 60 pages of US Department of Justice records and court documents concerning the proceeding to officials in the Trump administration, members of Congress and congressional staff.

The underlying case dates to 1993 and involved funds held in accounts linked to Tinubu.

Authentic US court records show that $460,000 associated with an account held in Tinubu’s name was forfeited to the United States government following a civil proceeding. The documents connected the forfeited funds to allegations involving narcotics proceeds and financial transactions covered by US money-laundering statutes.

However, the proceeding was a civil asset forfeiture case, not a criminal conviction of Tinubu for drug trafficking. AFP previously authenticated the court documents and reported that they did not show that Tinubu was indicted or convicted in the case.

That distinction has remained central to the political argument surrounding the records.

Atiku has repeatedly challenged the Presidency to explain the forfeiture rather than attack his Washington representatives. TheCable reported earlier this month that Atiku accused government officials of attempting to discredit Von Batten-Montague-York instead of addressing questions surrounding the historical proceeding.

Fani-Kayode, meanwhile, has strongly criticised Von Batten and rejected the lobbying firm’s portrayal of Tinubu.

In a September 8 article published by Premium Times, Fani-Kayode accused Von Batten of attempting to discredit the President and stressed that Tinubu had not been indicted or convicted of a crime in the United States. He also challenged the lobbyist to substantiate separate allegations concerning an alleged attempt to offer him $3 million to end his campaign against Tinubu.

Von Batten-Montague-York had earlier alleged that its founder received an unsolicited $3 million offer from a person it said was connected to Tinubu. The firm said it preserved the communications and intended to submit them to US authorities. No publicly cited evidence has independently established that the alleged offer came from Tinubu or his government.

The latest exchange has now shifted attention from the historical forfeiture records to the increasingly acrimonious confrontation between Fani-Kayode and Atiku’s lobbyists.

Von Batten said his firm would raise the alleged threat with US federal authorities. At the time of reporting, there was no public indication that an American law-enforcement agency had opened an investigation into the latest exchange.

The row comes as Nigeria approaches the 2027 presidential election, with Tinubu and Atiku among the candidates, giving the long-running dispute over the 1993 US records renewed political significance.

text:
🌽 WHAT THE ORGANIC SEAL ACTUALLY BUYS —
The Soil Remembers What the Rain Forgives 🏷️
🚧 THE BUFFER ZONE HAS NO NUMBER ▸ ▸ ▸ 📖 Post 11 OF 19
✅ Every certified organic field in the United States must have a buffer zone between it and adjoining land in conventional production. Federal regulation does not say how wide.

There is no number anywhere in the rule. On the other side of that same fence line, the conventional applicator is working to buffers specified on the pesticide label in distances running up to four hundred feet.

▸ ▸ ▸

Two requirements sit at 7 CFR 205.202, and together they are the entire perimeter defense of American organic agriculture.

Subsection (b) is the one everybody knows. Any field or farm parcel from which organic product is harvested must have had no prohibited substance applied to it for three years immediately preceding harvest.

Thirty-six months. The transition clock.

Subsection (c) is the one almost nobody knows. It requires the parcel to have distinct, defined boundaries and buffer zones — such as runoff diversions — to prevent the unintended application of a prohibited substance to the crop, or contact with a prohibited substance applied to adjoining land not under organic management.

🔒 Sufficient to prevent unintended contact. That is the entire standard. No distance, no formula, no minimum.

The definition at 205.2 is equally open. A buffer zone is an area between a certified operation and adjacent land not under organic management, which must be sufficient in size or other features — the regulation offers windbreaks and diversion ditches as examples — to prevent contact by prohibited substances applied to adjacent areas.

Sufficient. Established. By whom, and how big, the rule does not say.

▸ ▸ ▸

What fills that vacuum is the certifier.

Width is determined case by case by the accredited certifying agent, working from the operation's organic system plan and from conditions on the ground: prevailing wind, what the neighbor grows, how they apply it, whether there is a hedgerow, a treeline, a road or a ditch in between.

USDA's own guidance for operators points them to their certifier, and notes that many certifiers use fifty feet as a common starting width.

The published conventions spread out from there. Extension guidance for organic systems describes typical buffers of twenty-five to thirty feet. One organic certifier's grower guidelines recommend a minimum of fifty feet, reduced to thirty where a dense hedgerow exists, and require the buffer to be maintained for at least three years after the last prohibited application on the adjacent land.

Another organic organization's factsheet gives a working range of twenty-five to over one hundred feet depending on risk. Canada's standard specifies at least eight meters.

💡 The bottom line: the boundary between organic and conventional in the United States is drawn by the entity the farm hired to certify it, using a convention rather than a regulation, and the conventions do not agree with each other.

▸ ▸ ▸

Now hold that against what is happening on the other side of the line.

EPA regulates spray drift with actual numbers, published on pesticide labels and enforceable against the applicator. Downwind buffer distances vary by application method and by the potential for off-site impact, and the ranges are not small: aerial application from zero up to 320 feet, ground boom from zero up to 310 feet, airblast sprayers from zero up to 160 feet. Individual product labels go higher — some specify a 400-foot aerial buffer.

EPA also defines an Application Exclusion Zone of 100 feet for airblast equipment.

Then there is what was actually measured.

📊 A study published in the Annals of Work Exposures and Health in 2018 ran six spray trials with a conventional axial fan airblast sprayer in a working orchard. Researchers suspended 270 polyester line samplers on fifteen vertical masts downwind, applied zinc, molybdenum and copper micronutrient tracers, and analyzed the samples by mass spectrometry.

They found evidence of drift up to 52 meters downwind — roughly 170 feet, about 1.7 times the Application Exclusion Zone EPA defines for that equipment.

And drift is exquisitely sensitive to how the machine is set. Spray Drift Task Force data shows that raising nozzle height from eight feet to twenty-two puts roughly two and a half times more material on the ground twenty-five feet downwind.

⚠️ The regulated distance on the conventional side of the fence can exceed 300 feet. The convention on the organic side is fifty.

▸ ▸ ▸

That comparison is the heart of this post, and it needs one honest qualification.

EPA's buffers and organic's buffers are not measuring the same thing. EPA's are set to protect listed species and sensitive sites from a specific product at a specific rate, at the high end of a risk assessment. Most applications are not at the high end. Fifty feet against a ground application of a coarse-droplet product on a still day is genuinely adequate.

But the range is the point. A single national number would be wrong nearly everywhere — excessive against a hand-applied product in calm air, and grossly insufficient against aerial application in a crosswind. Certifier discretion, exercised by an inspector who has walked the property line, is a better instrument than a figure written in Washington.

That argument is correct as far as it goes.

It also means there is no floor. A discretionary standard administered by a paid agent has no minimum below which it cannot fall, and no mechanism by which a shopper can know which end of the range their food came from.

▸ ▸ ▸

The discretion does have teeth, and this is the part that argues for the system.

State certification guidance distinguishes passive from active buffer management. Passive means the distance and existing features are sufficient on their own. Active means they are not, and the operation must do something about it — divert the crop harvested from inside the boundary strip to the conventional market, destroy it by disking or mowing rather than harvesting it, or leave that ground unplanted entirely.

A certifier can require a farmer to plow under the outer rows of his own field.

That is a real enforcement power, routinely exercised, and it is invisible to everyone outside the certification relationship.

▸ ▸ ▸

And yet USDA's own residue study found chlorpyrifos on three organic apple samples and attributed it to drift from neighboring orchards.

That is 205.202(c) failing in exactly the manner it was written to prevent, documented by the agency that wrote it.

▸ ▸ ▸

There is a deeper problem underneath all of this, and the rest of the series exists to document it.

Both requirements at 205.202 describe a horizontal threat. Subsection (b) assumes contamination came from this soil's own past and will fade in three years. Subsection (c) assumes contamination arrives sideways, from the property next door, and can be stopped by putting distance between the two.

Neither assumption survives the evidence.

The soil does not clear in three years for every compound, and some compounds do not clear at all. And a great deal of what lands on an organic field did not come from the neighbor.

⚠️ A buffer zone has a width. It does not have a roof.

text:
You are correct. Jesus fulfilled the law. Righteousness, or “right standing” with God, is of God. God did it. God redeemed you to Himself. You are righteous in your spirit. Your body will return to dust, but your spirit is the real you and your soul (mind, will, and emotions) is connected to your spirit.

“But now the righteousness of God apart from the law is revealed, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets, even the righteousness of God, through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and on all who believe. For there is no difference; for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiation by His blood, through faith, to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance God had passed over the sins that were previously committed, to demonstrate at the present time His righteousness, that He might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus” (Rom 3:21-26).

Jesus paid a debt He did not owe, because we owed a debt we could not pay. Our debt was caused by the first Adam’s disobedience. God warned Adam he would die, and he did. Adam died spiritually, even though his body lived 930 years. "Therefore, as through one man’s offense (Adam) judgment came to all men, resulting in condemnation, even so through one Man’s (Jesus) righteous act the free gift came to all men, resulting in justification of life (Rom 5:18).

By man sin entered the world, and death through sin. So by Man death had to be defeated. But all humans inherit the sin nature Adam gained in his spirit. “Therefore, just as through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin, and thus spread to all men, because all sinned” (Rom 5:13). Jesus was an incarnation - God in Man. The seed of Mary was made pregnant by God the Holy Spirit to bypass the corrupt seed of Adam that was passed on to all humans. Jesus lived a perfect, sinless life, and that qualified Him to die for the sin of humankind. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so also by one Man’s obedience many will be made righteous" (Rom 5:19).

God put on Jesus on the cross all the sin and sickness of the entire human race, past, present, and future. He became SIN, which caused Him to die spiritually, and then three hours later He died physically. He became a blob on the cross. “Just as many were astonished at you, so His visage was marred more than any man, and His form more than the sons of men” (Is 52:14). Jesus said, “It is finished!” And bowing His head, He gave up His spirit” (Jn 19:30). In other words, His spirit left His body, but He had already lost the life of God from His spirit. He was separated from Father, which is why He cried, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Matt 27:46). The Bible does not contradict itself but one can get confused. The answers to the Bible are in the Bible.

Thus, the Law was “finished,” having been perfectly fulfilled by Jesus, who nailed it to His cross. “Having wiped out the handwriting of requirements that was against us, which was contrary to us. And He has taken it out of the way, having nailed it to the cross” (Col 2:14). The law was “against us” because it was impossible for anyone in a flesh body (except Jesus) to keep. Flesh is weak. But God’s plan of redemption was not yet completed; not until Jesus resurrected and put His blood in the heavenly Holy of Holies.

Jesus spent three days/nights in hell and preached to all the captives there. All who died before Jesus’ resurrection got a second chance; everyone in the Old Testament, plus some in the gospels like Judas Iscariot. “For Christ also died for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit; in which he went and preached to the spirits in prison” (1 Pet 3:18-19). That verse is full of revelation. It also shows that Jesus died both physically AND spiritually.

Since Jesus’ resurrection, under the New Covenant of grace, you only get one chance to believe in Him. You must make your choice before you die physically. “You must be born again” (John 3:7). Your spirit is the part of you that got born again. Can you feel God in your spirit? No. You must have faith and believe what the Bible says about you.

For three days/nights Jesus’ spirit was separated from Father, in hell. But the devil could not hold Him there. When God was satisfied that the debt was paid, God the Holy Spirit went down into hell and brought Jesus back to life. He appeared to Mary Magdalene and said, “Do not cling to Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father; but go to My brethren and say to them, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and to My God and your God.’” (John 20:17). Jesus still needed to put His blood in the tabernacle in heaven. “But Christ came as High Priest of the good things to come, with the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is, not of this creation. Not with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood He entered the Most Holy Place ONCE for all, having obtained eternal redemption” (Heb 9:11-12).

Jesus is our High Priest. “For if the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkling the unclean, sanctifies for the purifying of the flesh, how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without spot to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” (Heb 9:13-14). Why would you return to “dead works,” or trying to keep the law by your own effort, rather than receive the righteousness freely given to you from God? You are under a better covenant. “And for this reason He is the Mediator of the new covenant, by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, that those who are called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance” (Heb 9:15).

Grace is not an excuse to sin; it is the antidote for sin. The more you focus on the Lord and renew your mind, the less you will commit sin with your mind and body. But you will still sin. However, you cannot sin with your spirit, the part of you that is redeemed to God the Father. “For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them” (Eph 2:8-10). Your motivation for doing good works is what matters (the love of God in you, versus you trying to earn His blessing).

You are either “in Christ” (saved) or “in Adam” (unsaved) based on whether you accepted God’s free gift of salvation. If you believe in Jesus Christ, then you receive His righteousness (in your spirit - the part of you that is eternal), not because of anything you DO, but rather because of what He DID. Jesus is the first “God in Man” since the first Adam. You and I, and all Christians, are the umpteen billionth God in man, or God in woman. Adam and Eve lost the life of God from their spirits. But thanks to Jesus, we can’t lose Him. Thank You, Jesus.

text:
Metropolitan Gabriel Severos (1540 – 1616) on sin being a disease, baptism being a cure, and the whole purpose of Christ's Sacrifice being to cleanse, sanctify & reconcile us:

(Note: I put a lot of effort into researching this, and I finally found all four of Severos' most relevant works in Greek, although I am still unable to access the actual original primary material, as it is being gatekept by prestigious Greek libraries. Nevertheless, I found a copy of the works by Richard Simon, who translated it to Latin in 1671, but retained the Greek next to it. I was expecting the language to sound very scholastic and full of interpolations, since it was translated by a Papist, but to my surprise, the work reads almost exactly as you would expect a modern Orthodox author to be writing.)

On sin:
"As his flesh, after it had been washed seven times, was restored like the flesh of a little child and wholly purged, so we through the seven mysteries of the holy Church are turned back from our errors, and are restored and purified in the things we had lost. For after the fall we lost the God-given beauty —continual health, purity, strength, a pure conscience, liberty, piety, and the fervour of love toward God."
- This is in line with the Orthodox view of original sin, in this exhaustive enumeration we don't see anything which suggests inherited guilt or reatus. As we'll see throughout, the metaphysics of Severos are thoroughly participatory and remedial; which doesn't allow for a juridical account.

"All these our God, supremely merciful, deigned to restore to us through the seven mysteries. For we put off the deformity, that is the old man, in putting off our body, and take up again that divine robe through holy baptism. We drive away the disease and recover health [ἀποσοβοῦμεν τὴν νόσον καὶ ἀναλαμβάνομεν τὴν ὑγείαν]. In faith, says blessed Paul, we are sound. We wipe away impurity and resume purity... we recover strength and cast off foolish pride we recover liberty, for we are no longer slaves of sin we recover piety and put away shamelessness we recover love toward God, and stir up hatred against the Devil."

Why the Incarnation happened:
"When He saw that men would not come by these means to the knowledge of Himself, but preferred to serve created things rather than Him, moved with infinite mercy — for He could scarcely bear to see the human race oppressed by the tyranny of the devil —He sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law, who having taken the form of a servant redeemed them by His own blood... Moreover with spiritual arms also — the holy Sacraments — instituted that they might guard and protect themselves against their enemies, unto health and salvation, and also for the overthrow of that first sin of our first parent."

"He became the firstborn of the dead — not because He rose first, for Lazarus rose, and the man Elisha raised, and others before; but because He rose and dies no more. For death shall no longer have dominion over Him. 
...Whence He brought in the parable of the grain symbolically, exhibiting the resurrection and the common resurrection of all men: For as in Adam we all die, so in Christ, who is the new Adam, we all live."
- Severos cites here from 1 Cor. 15:22, which is consistent with the early Greek Patristic tradition.

Why sin happens post-baptism:
"Those who, being in the vineyard and labouring, fall miserably through the envy of the architect of evil (Satan) and the weakness of the flesh [φθόνῳ τοῦ ἀρχεκάκου καὶ τῇ τῆς σαρκὸς ἀσθενείᾳ], sin wounding them in various ways — whom holy Repentance, coming upon them, raises up and makes bold, and again nobly rouses to the labours of virtue."

On the oil with prayer:
"To the body it restores strength and vigour; to the soul, beyond doubt, it affords remission of the sins by which it is weakened, and at length slain."

On the Crucifixion:

"This victim the first and highest and only holy High Priest, our Lord Jesus Christ, offered — Himself, to God and the Father, on behalf of the whole of human nature [ὑπὲρ πάσης τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης φύσεως]."

"At that hour He was lifted up on the cross; then, bowing His head, He gave up the spirit; and He became the liturgist of His own self, sacrificing Himself on behalf of the whole of our nature [λειτουργὸς αὐτὸς ἑαυτοῦ γέγονεν, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὅλης φύσεως ἡμῶν θύσας ἑαυτόν]."
- The reason for why the Atonement happened according to Severos was in order to sanctify human nature. Christ did this on behalf of us, not in place of us. This is a mirroring of how Saints Athanasius and Cyril spoke about our Lord.

The Eucharist explains the Sacrifice:
"It is called an unbloody sacrifice — to distinguish it from the victims offered through blood; and it took this name from our Saviour, who became a victim for us. 'He delivered Himself for us an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness' [Eph. 5:2]."

"As the coal burns, purges, illuminates, so also the sanctified bread converted into our Saviour's flesh. It burns those who partake of it unworthily, for it is to them unto judgement, according to blessed Paul. It purges and consumes the sins of the faithful who share in it — the blood of Jesus, says John, cleanses us from all sin. It illuminates and irradiates the mind of those who bring it into the house of their soul."

- Fides Ecclesiae Orientalis, seu Gabrielis Metropolitae Philadelphiensis opuscula, nunc primum de Graecis conversa
